readingBehavior.dpdp: Purpose is a machined compass with 48 tick marks and five data tiles. Notice is an opening book with layered pages, leather covers, spine, bookmark and brass corners. Consent is a beveled console with two independent switches and recorded-choice indicators. Withdrawal uses separating keyed plugs, copper-colored pins and rubber cables. Children uses an arched guardian portal with two figurines, lock and gate. Responsibility is an inset vault with wheel, hinges and locking bolts. Evidence is a layered archive with backing, rivets, an Example seal and three labelled evidence nodes. The orb and its rings appear only in the Overview hero. The DPDP overview hero uses two equal columns, 2rem gap, 64px top/52px bottom padding and a 720px minimum height. Its 470px-high model anchors notice, choice, safeguards and evidence in one overview. Below 1000px the hero stacks and its stage becomes 390px tall. The seven mounted scene articles form a scroll-stacking tile gallery on hydrated desktop layouts with motion enabled. Zero-height natural-flow markers track the original chapter positions. Sticky tiles start at 164px plus 10px per chapter, with increasing z-index, 140px trailing spacing, a 1400px gallery perspective and top-centered transforms. Previous tiles shrink from 1 to 0.92 and tilt from 0 to -2 degrees as scrolling advances; their covered controls become inert. For viewport heights from 701px to 850px, chapter offsets narrow to 6px, panel padding becomes 20px and model stages become 280px tall. Compact layouts, heights at most 700px, reduced motion and SSR retain ordinary reading flow. A ResizeObserver also measures each tile against its sticky top and a 16px viewport reserve. If any tile cannot fit, including an expanded withdrawal history, the journey switches to ordinary reading flow even above the compact breakpoints. A layout effect preserves the active chapter at a 140px reading offset; viewport resizing retries the stack. Desktop scene panels use 1.05fr/1fr columns, a 32px to 90px gap, 490px minimum height and 36px corners. At widths of 1100px and above, even panels reverse the visual and copy; each visual stays within its own panel. Stage heights are 410px desktop and 350px below 1000px. Progression sticks at 80px desktop and 64px compact and scrolls horizontally when necessary. Widths below 768px and viewport heights at most 700px use stacked, auto-height panels and 280px model stages with real Three.js renders. These layout thresholds no longer disable WebGL. Reduced motion, SSR/pre-hydration, no JavaScript and WebGL failure show diagrams with the same DOM controls. Native detail windows are at most 560px wide, viewport width minus 32px, and 85dvh tall. The complete reference remains one native disclosure containing thirteen continuous chapter articles, with chapter hash links and a full-guide open/close control. The contact speech bubble is hidden on this page. Other legal readers, plan details and shared forms become one column at 760px; legal reading uses a 230px index and 64px gap, articles a 210px index and 48px gap, stacking at 800px. The article library combines a featured story with two columns of bordered rows, becoming one column at 800px. Pricing pairs a 280px plan index with a two-column detail area and a complete comparison disclosure. The DPDP guide uses PrivacyHero plus PrivacyJourney: eight independent stages, with an overview followed by purpose, notice, consent, withdrawal, children, responsibility and evidence. Each article stays mounted and its canvas stays inside its panel. Motion reads its natural-flow marker from 160px to -640px and smooths tile scale/tilt with a stiffness-180/damping-36 spring. Active-chapter tracking uses passive scroll and resize listeners scheduled through requestAnimationFrame. Named progression buttons scroll to the original marker and sticky offset, so navigation does not jump to a displaced sticky article. Covered tiles are inert. Desktop stacking mode limits live stages to the active and next chapter within the viewport gate; ordinary reading flow uses the viewport gate alone. The bottom summary shows optional paths and written notice/choice/record explanations. Raycast selection has equivalent DOM buttons, with object descriptions, legal notes and the example evidence record in PrivacyInfoWindow. A pale-sage outline identifies keyboard focus. Legacy privacy-journey.css remains a shared base; privacy-experience.css overrides its earlier travelling-stage layout and type rules. Notice unfolds into two labelled 3D pages, "Your data" and "The purpose". Pointer raycasting and equivalent DOM buttons inspect the notice, guardian gate and three evidence plates labelled Notice, Choice and Time. The responsibility scene uses an inset vault labelled Safeguards, with a locking wheel, hinges and bolts. Object and chapter explanations open a native `dialog` with browser focus containment, Escape and close controls, backdrop dismissal, body scroll lock and restoration of the previously focused trigger. Modals contain fuller prose while scene captions stay short. Scroll moves the compass needle and data tiles, unfolds the notice book, turns the vault wheel and adjusts stage depth and lighting; pointer movement tilts the camera. The consent switches and withdrawal plugs settle from the existing bounded recorded-choice state. Draft choices do not activate optional paths. Frames stop after settling and pause when hidden. Physically based enamel, dark metal, brass, ivory and rubber materials use studio environment reflections from RoomEnvironment/PMREM, ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure 0.9 and restrained key/fill lighting. The reflection target is disposed with geometry, materials, textures, renderer and context. In desktop stacking mode, only the active and next chapter may mount a live stage within an 80px viewport margin. In normal reading flow, each stage uses the viewport gate alone, so mobile and short viewports render the real Three.js figures when visible, enabled and motion is allowed. Distant stages release their resources. Rendering density is capped at 1.25 below 768px and 1.5 on desktop, recalculated by ResizeObserver; canvas touch-action is pan-y. Disposal includes textures, geometry, materials, event listeners, renderer and context. WebGL failure retains diagrams and equivalent DOM controls. Every demonstration remains in page memory and calls no API or actual consent service. Page-memory draft/record/withdraw/reset keeps at most twelve history events and never reactivates current consent through history inspection. Full thirteen-chapter reference and legal caveats retained.

narrative.overview:
This descriptive shorthand records the user-approved enterprise direction: navy navigation, neutral working surfaces, precise teal selection, and restrained Motion interactions. Retain the Consent Guru name and logo. Evidence and configuration should remain readable in ordinary controls, tables, timelines, and the 2D graph.

The public website uses Manrope with generous space and curved surfaces. The DPDP guide pairs ivory, sage and deep green with Instrument Serif italic accents in an interactive privacy exhibit: one overview hero and seven fixed scene models for purpose, notice, consent, withdrawal, children, responsibility and evidence. Short captions sit beside the models; compact native modal windows hold object explanations, chapter notes and the example evidence record. A single native disclosure opens all thirteen legal chapters in continuous reading flow. Articles, learning and pricing retain their respective outlines, manual decks and reading controls. Dashboard tools share contextual navigation, task tabs and guidance alongside fields. Optional 3D exploration supplements the dependency map.

The latest pinned request in `.impeccable/ui-direction.md` asks why mobile lacks the 3D figures. Mobile and short viewports now render the Three.js complete-flow hero and seven distinct chapter models in ordinary reading flow; the established desktop stack, fixed panels, minimal captions, compact detail windows and professional curved green/ivory presentation remain the composition contract. Its five-block contract records thesis, typography, palette and material, composition, and interaction. The earlier session seed `fd4b7635` is provenance, not an approved image comp; no image comp or separate QUALITY BAR card was approved. The north star above is descriptive shorthand for the requested enterprise appearance.
keyCharacteristics: Navy navigation and teal action emphasis.
Optional spatial exploration with a readable map and list.
Natural scroll storytelling with complete legal content available.
Manrope reading typography, selective serif italics and broad curved story panels.

rules.name: The Provenance Rule
rules.body: Pair provenance color with a written label; color alone must not imply proof or enforcement.

rules.name: The Unique Model Rule
rules.body: Give every DPDP chapter its own detailed object and mechanism; reserve the orb and rings for the Overview hero.

dos: **Do** reuse scoped theme variables and existing logo assets.
**Do** preserve written provenance, visible focus, and readable alternatives to 3D.
**Do** use Motion for short user-triggered state changes and honor reduced motion.
**Do** distinguish fixture screenshots and illustrative public diagrams from live evidence.
**Do** preserve public factual copy, pricing terms, links, and legal content.
donts: **Don't** add decorative continuous motion or motion that steers consent choices.
**Don't** invent metrics, evidence, enforcement status, or backend capabilities.
**Don't** hide graph truncation limits or make 3D the only inspection path.
**Don't** assume public fixed-color sections automatically support dashboard dark tokens.
